Metabolic Flux Analysis Ontology is an ontology that provides a structured framework for representing concepts, relationships, and data related to metabolic flux analysis.

definition.val: An information content entity that represents the complete set of metabolic fluxes (reaction rates) in a biological system.
An information content entity that contains files to determine the rates of metabolic reactions.

comments: It generally includes the model of metabolic networks and experimental data.

definition.val: A metabolic flux of a metabolic reaction that occurs within a metabolic network model boundries.
A metabolic flux that is the rate of a transport process.
A chemical or physical process within a biological entity that is part of the metabolism.
A quality of a biochemical reaction which may proceed simultaneously in forward and backward direction.
A quality of metabolic reaction to proceed in forward and backward direction.

comments: property could be True or False

definition.val: The chemical reaction that solely operates in a single direction, it can be forward or backward direction.

comments: property or class

definition.val: The chemical reaction that may operate simultaneously in forward and backward direction.
A quality of the chemical reaction that shows direction of the reaction operates, which is determined by the Gibbs free energy change.
The chemical reaction that proceeds from reactants to products.
The chemical reaction that proceeds from products to reactants.

The realizable entity that is realized when the reactants and products of the chemical process are present in concentrations which have no further tendency to change with time, so that there is no observable change in the properties of the system.

comments: At equilibrium, the reaction Gibbs energy is zero.

definition.val: A metabolite which is only consumed, typically the substrate(s).
A metabolite which is only produced, typically the by-product(s).
The system biology representation that is based on quantitative visualization of reactions and metabolic fluxes within a metabolic network.

basicPropertyValues.val: The flux map is typically scaled by flux magnitude and annotated with directionality.

definition.val: A fluxome that indicates specific pattern or distribution of metabolic fluxes within a biological system, such as a cell or organism, under defined conditions.
The metabolic flux anlaysis method based on mathemetical approaches for characterizing metabolic states that constrain the possible flux space given a reaction stoichiometry.

The stoichiometry-based fluxomics method that uses set of mathematical approaches in which the possible fluxes are constrained by a minimum and maximum range of bounds, and further restrictions such as the reaction stoichiometry or objectives.
A metabolic flux analysis method that determines metabolic fluxes within a cell based on empirical data.
A plan specification that quantitatively estimate/infer metabolic fluxes using a metabolic reaction model, experimental data and computation.
An information content entity that contains set of all possible flux vectors that are consistent with reaction stoichiometries and a set of flux constraints at metabolic steady state.
The data item with a list of the rates of all chemical reactions in a biological network.
A representation of chemical or biological networks that uses the quantitative relationships (stoichiometry) between reactants and products.
The reaction rate at which a specific chemical reaction proceeds from reactants to products.

comments: non-negative

definition.val: The reaction rate at which a specific reaction proceeds from products to reactants.

comments: non-negative

definition.val: The reaction rate that denotes the difference between the forward and backward flux for a chemical reaction.
The reaction rate that denotes the minimum of the forward and backward fluxes of a chemical reaction.

comments: non-negative; This is different from exchange flux in flux balance analysis (make note in ontology)

definition.val: The data item that represents the relative proportion of metabolic flow directed into a specific pathway at a divergence point compared to the total flow or an alternative route at that same junction.

nodes.lbl: degrees of freedom in stoichiometry matrix

definition.val: A number of degrees of freedom that represents the number of free/independent fluxes that can be varied independently within the network, which is determined by the null space of the stoichiometric matrix.

comments: The dimension of this null space gives the number of fluxes needed to define all other fluxes.

definition.val: A molecule that has the same atomic composition (molecular formula) but different line formulae or different stereochemical formulae and hence different physical and/or chemical properties.
A data item that is the specific distribution of istopic atom in a metabolite pools at specific time.

The information content entity that describes the rate of change of an intracellular metabolite concentration is considered negligible, which holds when the metabolic flux through the metabolite pools is much larger than the change in their pool sizes over time.
A steady state in which both metabolic fluxes and intracellular metabolite pool sizes are approximately constant over time.
A process of an isotopic labeling experiment where metabolite labeling patterns are not yet constant.
A steady state when the distribution of a stable isotope label within a biological system has become and remains constant over time.
A fluxomics simulation that performs stochastic process for characterizing the range of possible/feasible metabolic flux vectors.
A completely executed planned process that studies the metabolic fluxes of the reactions in a metabolic network.
The fluxomics investigation that predicts physiological phenotypes allowed by the underlying metabolic model, typically enforced by a metabolic goal (e.g., maximize growth rate).

The fluxomics investigation that employs a quantitative strategy based on a metabolic network and experimental data to determine intracellular reaction rates (fluxes) with the highest possible accuracy.
The metabolic flux analysis method that used to measure the rates of intracellular metabolic reactions in living cells using data from isotope labeling experiments.
The isotope-based metabolic flux analysis that estimates metabolic fluxes by tracking from the distribution of 13C isotopes in metabolites.

nodes.lbl: isotopically stationary metabolic flux analysis method

definition.val: The isotope-based metabolic flux analysis assumes isotopic steady state and metabolic steady state.

nodes.lbl: isotopically non-stationary metabolic flux analysis method

definition.val: The isotope-based metabolic flux analysis that assumes isotopic transient state and metabolic steady state.

nodes.lbl: dynamic Isotope-based metabolic flux analysis method

definition.val: The isotope-based metabolic flux analysis that assumes both isotopic and metabolic dynamic state.
The experimental design and studies that aims to increase the information content of an isotope labeling experiment.
The isotope labeling experiment design that achieves targeted improvement of the information gain of an isotope labeling experiment.
The isotope labeling experiment design that strategically choose isotopic tracers (molecule, labeling position, isotope) based on target pathway thermodynamics and atom transitions.
A fluxoimcs assay where biological entities are fed stable isotopic tracers (like 13C) which are then distributed throughout the metabolic network via metabolic activity.
The fluxomics isotope labeling experiment where different isotopic tracers with distinct labeling patterns or tracer mixtures are supplied to resolve overlapping metabolic routes.
A fluxomics isotope labeling experiment where a single tracer or tracer mixture is supplied.
A molecular entity that is an electrically charged product of reaction of a particular parent ion.

comments: In general such ions have a direct relationship to a particular precursor ion and indeed may relate to a unique state of the precursor ion. The reaction need not necessarily involve fragmentation. It could, for example, involve a change in the number of charges carried. Thus, all fragment ions are daughter ions, but not all daughter ions are necessarily fragment ions.

definition.val: A molecular entity that is an electrically charged molecular moiety which may dissociate to form fragments, one or more of which may be electrically charged, and one or more neutral species.

comments: A parent ion may be a molecular ion or an electrically charged fragment of a molecular ion.

definition.val: An isotopologue distribution that is of the relative abundance of different isotopomers in both a parent molecule and its fragments, obtained through tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS).
An isotopic information that is the percentage of molecules in a given metabolite pool that contain one or more isotopic labels from a tracer.

basicPropertyValues.val: e.g. it can be represented using cumonomer representation as "x1x/(x0x + x1x)".

definition.val: A zero-dimensional temporal region where a sample is taken from the biological experiment for analysis.

A model parameter estimation that runs a metabolic flux analysis method on a metabolic network model and/or experimental data using a fluxomics software, producing a flux solution and associated statistics.
A three-dimensional spatial region that is a physically or functionally distinct space (e.g., Cytosol, Mitochondria, Metabolon).

basicPropertyValues.val: Maybe change name to biological compartment or cellular compartment

definition.val: A system biology representation that defines the stoichiometric representation of cellular macromolecules (e.g. Protein, DNA, RNA, Lipids).
A system biology representation that is a set of one or several metabolites.
A system biology representation that is a metabolite pool in the metabolic network that does not have any biological counterpart and is purely introduced for modeling reason.
An data entity that is an amount of molecular entity available to a particular metabolic process.
A system biology representation that the aggregate of metabolic reactions in a metabolic network model.
A molecule property where certain atoms are chemically indistinguishable, making a unique atom numbering impossible.
A system biology representation that models a metabolic reaction that does not have any biological counterpart.
A lumped reaction is a simplified reaction that merge multiple chemical reactions into a single reaction for modeling reason.
A pseudo metabolic reaction that is an abstract reaction that represents consumption of metabolites for cellular growth in a metabolic model.
A mathematical expression that represents the limits on metabolic flux value on reactions.
An identifier that is a unique position to atoms in a molecule to track its position within the molecule.
A representation that is the precise mapping of how each relevant atom in a substrate is rearranged to form the product metabolites during a reaction. It usually excludes hydrogens.
An object aggregate that is made of atom transitions for all reactions making up a metabolic network model.

basicPropertyValues.val: Not a material entity. Systems biology representation

definition.val: The identifier that records the annotation types for atom transition.
An atom transition annotation that uses a-z and A-Z to represent the order of the tracked atoms in a molecule.
An atom transition annotation that uses FluxML definition to track atom mapping in a reaction.
An atom transition annotation that uses InChI specification to track atoms in a reaction.
An atom transition annotation that uses SMILE specification to track atoms in a reaction.
An atom transition that represents the complementary atom transition in a reaction that involves symmetric compound.
An object aggregate that is made of differentially labeled substrate isotopomers (e.g., % [1-¹³C]glucose + % [U-¹³C]glucose) administered in an ILE.

synonyms.val: commercial isotopically labelled molecular entity mixture

definition.val: The quality that defines the characteristics of the isotopic tracer.
An isotopic tracer property that is the chemical purity specified in the label input.

Could be changed to "Chemical purity" and moved up

definition.val: A fluxomics parameter that is required to execute fluxomics software for a fluxomics investigation.
A measurement datum that measures the rate of biomass formation.

basicPropertyValues.val:
Te: Isn't this a quality? refer to PATO:0001492
Sergi: I don't think so, it's a number measuring how fast cells are growing. A quality does not require any process to be realized according to definition, and growth rate depends on a lot of factors and other stuff. If this was max growth rate, ir would be a realizable entity.

definition.val: A growth rate that measures the biomass increase per unit of existing biomass per unit of time.
A measurement datum that represents the efficiency of substrate conversion into product/biomass (mass or molar basis).
A statistic that measures the gap between observed values and model predictions, and unlike ordinary least squares, it assigns a specific weight to each data point.

basicPropertyValues.val: It is used in flux estimation, specifically the variance-weighted sum of squares residuals, which is minimized to quantify fluxes. It serves as a key indicator of goodness-of-fit to reflect the certainty with which metabolic fluxes were determined.

definition.val: A data transformation that used to obtain labeling data from a given metabolic models and presumed fluxes/metabolite concentrations.
A model parameter estimation that quantifies metabolic fluxes including their uncertainties.
A statistical mdoel that is to describe how to compute a labeling measurement based on the simulated labeling state space.

comments: It is usually represented as a matrix.

definition.val: A measurement value of a measured quantity as obtained by a forward simulation of the metabolic network model.
A statistical model that is to calculate the measurement standard deviation of a simulated measurement.
A matrix that is used to remove the contribution of naturally occurring heavy isotopes (e.g., 13C, 15N, 18O) from raw mass spectrometry data.
Lumped measurements are the measurements corresponding to the linear combination of two or more metabolites.
A fluxomics model parameter that is not of primary interest but must be included to correctly define the model and analyze the parameters that are of interest.
A nuisance parameter that is to model residual naturally labeled tracer in an input pool.
A nuisance parameter that is to account for residual naturally labeled fractions in a measurement group.
A mathematical expression that represents a criterion value for a proposed experimental design.
An XML format that is defined by FluxML specification for modeling metabolic flux analysis.
A data format specification for creating, validating, and exchanging metabolic flux analysis models in 13CFlux Software.

comments: It is designed with the aim of providing a standard document format for creating, validating and reliable exchanging of arbitrary metabolic models across different simulation tools.

definition.val: A data format specification that is a tabular text-based file format specification for defining metabolic reaction networks and isotopic labeling data used in 13C metabolic flux analysis.

comments: The format is obsolete.

definition.val: A data format specification for metabolic tracer flux data exchange in metabolic flux analysis for Influx_si software.
A software designed to perform, support, or facilitate metabolic flux computations.
The fluxomics software specifically designed to quantitatively estimate intracellular metabolic fluxes from an isotopic metabolic flux analysis investigation.
A metabolic flux analysis software that is a MATLAB-based software for estimating TCA cycle fluxes from 13C NMR isotopomer data (Chance et al., J Biol Chem, 1983; Malloy et al., Am J Physiol, 1990).

comments: SIM performs forward simulation of isotopic labeling in the citric acid cycle; tcaCALC performs flux calculation by fitting simulated isotopomer patterns to observed NMR data.

definition.val: A metabolic flux analysis software that is a universal software framework for 13C-based metabolic flux analysis that supports modeling, simulation, design, evaluation, and statistical analysis of 13C-labeling experiments using a cumomer-based simulation approach (Wiechert et al., Metab Eng, 2001, DOI: 10.1006/mben.2001.0188).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is a third-generation, high-performance simulator supporting both isotopically stationary and non-stationary 13C-MFA, featuring dual EMU/cumomer representations, multi-isotope tracer support, Bayesian uncertainty quantification, and a Python API (Stratmann et al., Bioinformatics, 2025, DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf630).

A metabolic flux analysis software that for estimating metabolic fluxes from stationary isotopic labeling data using the NLSIC algorithm, which provides more reliable convergence and better numerical accuracy than other optimization methods (Sokol et al., Bioinformatics, 2012, DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/bts705).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is an extended version of influx_s that handles isotopically non-stationary labeling experiments, sharing the same NLSIC fitting algorithm and input/output formats with unconditional stability during ODE solving (Sokol et al., Bioinformatics, 2012, DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/bts705).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is an updated MATLAB-based 13C MFA software building on the INCA platform, supporting both steady-state and isotopically non-stationary MFA with the EMU framework, parallel labeling experiments, and improved computational capabilities (Young, Bioinformatics, 2014, DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btu015).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is an open-source MATLAB-based software for both conventional and isotopically nonstationary 13C-MFA, featuring auto-generation of metabolic models from Excel configuration worksheets and using the Levenberg-Marquardt method for flux estimation (Kajihata et al., BioMed Res Int, 2014, DOI: 10.1155/2014/627014).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is an open-source Python package for 13C-MFA supporting the EMU framework, INST-MFA, parallel labeling experiments, and a Bayesian Metropolis-Hastings approach, providing flexibility for custom analysis workflows and experimental design via simulation (Matsuda et al., Metab Eng Commun, 2021, DOI: 10.1016/j.mec.2021.e00177).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is an extended version of OpenFLUX with support for parallel labeling experiments, extended statistical analysis, structural identifiability analysis, Monte Carlo confidence interval estimation, and experimental design optimization (Shupletsov et al., Microb Cell Fact, 2014, DOI: 10.1186/s12934-014-0152-x).
A metabolic flux analysis software that is a Scilab-based open-source software for 13C metabolic flux analysis that provides tools for isotopomer modeling and flux estimation.

A metabolic flux analysis software that is a MATLAB-based 13C MFA software with graphical user interface that supports steady-state 13C-MFA with user-friendly data input and flux visualization (He et al., Biotechnol Bioeng, 2016, DOI: 10.1002/bit.25958).
A metabolic flux analysis software that is a Python-based software package for stationary 13C metabolic flux analysis to estimate intracellular flux distributions.

A metabolic flux analysis software that is an EMU-based isotope simulator that uses adjacency matrix representation to efficiently simulate isotopic labeling patterns, enabling rapid forward simulation of mass isotopomer distributions for metabolic flux analysis and experimental design (Wu et al., Front Microbiol, 2019, DOI: 10.3389/fmicb.2019.00922).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is a Python package for 13C metabolic flux analysis at both isotopic steady state and transient state, supporting flux estimation, labeling pattern simulation, flux balance/variability analysis, and 15N labeling data (Wu et al., ACS Synth Biol, 2023, DOI: 10.1021/acssynbio.3c00265).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is a MATLAB-based software that formulates isotope-assisted MFA as an equality-constrained nonlinear program, improving scalability and robustness compared to traditional formulations (Lugar and Sriram, PLOS Comput Biol, 2022, DOI: 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009831).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is a web-based server for INST-13C MFA with standardized and visual flux analysis, using evolutionary optimization in parallel and providing real-time visualization of the flux optimization process (Liu et al., Bioinformatics, 2022, DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btac341).

A metabolic flux analysis software that is an open-source software library for Bayesian genome-scale 13C metabolic flux analysis, using MCMC Bayesian inference with COBRApy for handling genome-scale models and supporting Two Scale 13C MFA (Backman et al., PLOS Comput Biol, 2023, DOI: 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011111).
A data format specification for defining metabolic models and experimental data used by the FreeFlux software package.
A data format specification for defining metabolic models and experimental data used by the INCA software package.
A data item which represents the speed of a metabolic reaction.

comments: it is commonly refer to flux in MFA, even though formally it is a rate. The actual definition of metabolic flux is the amount of metabolite which is converted per time unit. It is calculated as the reaction rate times stoichiometric coefficient, often normalized to a specific quantity (e.g. cell dry weight or volume of a compartment)

definition.val: The metabolic flux of a metabolic reaction that occurs across metabolic network model boundaries.

comments: In the FBA field, the exchange flux means the external flux.

definition.val: A system biology representation that is a model representation of metabolism, which describes the biochemical reactions occurring within a cell or organism, connecting its genome to its physiology.
A process that is the set of physical or chemical processes that occur within a living organism in order to maintain life.
A metabolic model that represents a set of interconnected pathways of metabolic reactions within a biological entity.
A metabolic reaction that is the transfer of a metabolite or metabolites between two compartments.
A system biology representation that is an imaginary construct of a molecular entity that exist purely for modeling reasons (e.g. biomass).
A exchange flux that represents the minimum of the forward and backward fluxes of a chemical reaction, calculated by convention as a/(1+a), where a is the exchange flux.
An isotopologue that differs only in isotopic composition by a single element (e.g. 13C-1-glucose and 13C-2-glucose).

basicPropertyValues.val: In MS, this is the output of the natural isotope abundance correction.

definition.val: An isotopic tracer property that denotes the labelled chemical element for the fluxomics investigation (e.g. Carbon in a 13C labelled molecular entity).
A data entity that describes the total number of heavy particles (protons and neutrons jointly called nucleons) in the atomic nucleus.

comments: Symbol m in mass spectrometry.

basicPropertyValues.val: Duplicate of monoisotopic molecular mass. Maybe make it broad synonym?

definition.val: A molecular entity with isotopic tracer at specific atom number(s).
An isotopically labelled molecular entity that is the market version of the isotopically labelled molecule with manufacturer, purity and cost properties.

basicPropertyValues.val: e.g. the purchased [1-¹³C]glucose with purity of 99 atom % 13C.

definition.val: An isotopic information that is the input of the labelled source for the metabolic network model.
An isotopic tracer property that specifies the atom number of the isotopic tracer in the isotopically labelled molecular entity.
An isotopic tracer property that is the percentage of isotopically labelled molecular entity in a labelled source.
An isotopic tracer property that specifies the purity of the isotopic tracer in the commercial isotopically labelled molecular entity.

basicPropertyValues.val: e.g. the isotopic purity for 1,2-13C-Glucose is 99% on position 1 and 2.

definition.val: An isotopic information that is the average fraction of isotopically labeled atoms in a metabolite pool, calculated as the weighted sum of isotopologue abundances divided by the maximum possible number of label incorporations.

comments: Pierre: An average content of isotopic tracer element in the molecule that is calculated from isotopologue distribution.

definition.val: An information entity that contains details necessary to describe isotope or isotopologue information.
An isotopic information that describes the isotopic content of the molecule.

basicPropertyValues.val: e.g. percentage of 1,13C-Glucose in the total pool of Glucose in labbel input.

definition.val: An isotopic information that is the relative abundances of molecule isotopologues.
An isotopic information that is the abundance of isotopomers relative to the abundance of the complete set or subset of isotopic species.
An isotopic information that is the abundance of cumomer relative to the abundance of the complete set or subset of isotopic species.
A representation that is of isotopic state of a metabolite.
A representation that is the space of all isotopic forms of a metabolite.
An isotopic state-space representation that models positional labeling by a binary number (0: non-labeled, 1: labeled).
An isotopic state-space representation that models positional labeling by a state based on three possibilities: 0 represents unlabeled, 1 represents labeled or x: either labeled or unlabeled.
An isotopic state-space representation that models the mass differences due to labeling of a compound fragment. The fragment is defined by a binary number (position is/is not part of the fragment).
A measurement datum that measures the number of a particular countable entity.
A linear flux constraint that is the fixed value for linear combination of fluxes.
A linear flux constraint that represents the upper or lower bound of linear combinations of fluxes.
A representation that consists of a set of all atom identifiers considered for a molecule.
The representation that records the precise bijection of how each relevant atom identifier in a substrate is rearranged to form the product during a reaction.
A statistic that is the inherent variability of repeated observation measurements of a quantity including quantities evaluated by statistical methods and by other means.
A metabolic flux analysis method that is used to quantify the flux uncertainty estimate.
A statistic that quantify the uncertainty of the flux solution.
A data entity that specifies the parameters including flux vector and other parameters (e.g. metabolite pool sizes and model parameters) that best explains experimental data.
A fluxomics parameter that are necessary to run fluxomics labeling simulation.
A nuisance parameter that is to scale measurements of a measurement group to better fit simulated measurements.
A completely executed planned process that aims at quantifying the fluxes of molecules in biological entities.
A external flux indicating the rate of absorption of a molecular entity by a cell system from its surroundings.
A external flux indicating the rate of release of a metabolite by a cell system to its surroundings.
A metabolic model that represents a series of connected metabolic reactions.
A process which uses or consumes chemical/molecular entities to generate other molecular entities.
A reaction participant that is present at the start of a reaction and is consumed in the reaction.

comments: It usually sits on the left side of the reaction equation.

definition.val: A role of a molecule or pseudo molecule which is acted upon by an enzyme.
A role of a molecule or pseudo molecule which is produced from a chemical reaction.

comments: It usually sits on the right side of the reaction equation.

definition.val: A material entity that is an electrically neutral entity consisting of more than one atom.

basicPropertyValues.val: Must be electrically neutral and must consist of more than one atom bonded together.

definition.val: A material entity that is any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity.
A role of a molecule that is of any intermediate or product resulting from metabolism.

basicPropertyValues.val: The term 'metabolite' subsumes the classes commonly known as primary and secondary metabolites.

definition.val: A matrix that is a representation of a metabolic network, with rows representing metabolites and columns representing reactions. Each value indicates the stoichiometric coefficients, metabolites that are consumed are negative values and produced are positive values.
An isomer that differs only in isotopic composition (number of isotopic substitutions).
An isomer that is having the same number of each isotopic atom but differing in their positions.
A processed material entity that a isotope of the tracer element which are easily detectable due to their nuclear properties,

basicPropertyValues.val: It is used in fluxomics investigation. (e.g. 13C in a 13C labelled molecular entity).
It is used in various fields to study scientific problems by tracing the source, composition, distribution, and fate of elements or compounds.

definition.val: a state or condition of a system or process (such as one of the energy states of an atom) that does not change in time concerned.

basicPropertyValues.val: A cell where metabolite concentration are stable in time has reached a steady state
A realiable entity that takes place when a system has some parts or processes of interest that do not change over time.
A realizable entity that takes place when an entity has reached equilibrium for the measurement or phenomenon concerned.

definition.val: A planned process that is intended to test a hypothesis, and describe or explain empirical data obtained under various experimental conditions.
A fluxomics isotope labeling experiment in which isotopically labelled compounds are supplied to a biological system until the ratio of marked to unmarked molecules stabilizes at a constant level.

An fluxomics isotope labeling experiment that measures the rate at which isotopically labelled compounds are incorporated into cellular metabolites over time, specifically before the system reaches a stable isotopic equilibrium.
A material entity that is a maximal functionally integrated unit that develops from a program encoded in a genome
An organism that is genetically different from others of the same species and possessing a set of defined characteristics.
A data entity that records the number of atoms of the tracer element in this metabolite.
A processed material that provides the needed nourishment for microorganisms or cells grown in vitro.
A role that is a molecule participating in a reaction as reactant or product with an associated stoichiometric coefficient.
A device which is used to measure the mass to charge ratio of ions, and it consists of three basic parts: an ion source, a mass analyzer, and a detector system.

comments: The stages within the mass spectrometer are: 1. Production of ions from the sample 2. Separation of ions with different masses 3. Detection of the number of ions of each mass produced 4.Collection of data to generate the mass spectrum

definition.val: A device which is used to carry out a nuclear magnetic resonance analysis of some sample.
A systematic study of metabolites, the chemical processes they are involved, and the chemical fingerprints of specific cellular processes in a whole cell, tissue, organ or organism.

Proteomics is in the narrow sense (sensu stricto) the application of methods to separate, characterise, identify, and quantify all proteins (the proteome) - or a substantial set of proteins - that are present in a sample.

comments: Proteomics in the broad sense is the science of proteins and peptides on the large scale.

definition.val: A plan specification that is a spectrometry where the sample is converted into gaseous ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

A mass spectrometry method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being converted into ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.
A mass spectrometry method where a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography then ionised and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.
A mass spectrometry method that is involving multiple mass-selection steps, with some form of fragmentation occurring between each stage.
A mass spectrometry method where the relative abundance of isotopes in a sample is determined.

A plan specification that is a method to measure the energy states of spin-active nuclei placed in a static magnetic field are interrogated by inducing transitions between the states via radio frequency irradiation.

A data transformation which aims to take into account the contribution of natural random variation in isotopic composition in the environment and adjust for it during the calculation of mass isotopologue distribution in a tracer based metabolomics experiment.
A measurement datum that measures the amount of solute dissolved in a unit quantity of solvent or solution.

comments: It describes the strength or intensity of a solution in terms of its solute content. It is therefore a ratio in which the numerator is a measure of the solute and the denominator is a measure of the solvent.

definition.val: A representation that is an entity used in a systems biology knowledge reconstruction, such as a model, pathway, network.
A representation that is a specification of a chemical structure.
A data item that represents the net charge of a molecule.
A pseudo metabolic reaction that represents the reaction operating upon the internal metabolites.

comments: Metabolites that are consumed by these reactions are assumed to be used in intra-cellular processes that are not part of the model. Demand reactions, often represented 'R_DM_', can also deliver metabolites (from intra-cellular processes that are not considered in the model).

definition.val: A pseudo metabolic reaction that provides influx or efflux across a model boundary, for example replenishes a metabolic network with raw materials (eg carbon / energy sources).

comments: Such reactions are conceptual, created solely for modeling purposes, and do not have a physical correspondence. Exchange reactions, often represented as 'R_EX_', can operate in the negative (uptake) direction or positive (secretion) direction. By convention, a negative flux through an exchange reaction represents uptake of the corresponding metabolite, and a positive flux represent discharge.

definition.val: A pseudo metabolic reaction that is an unbalanced, typically reversible reaction used to add or remove intracellular metabolites from the system.

comments: It is typically a reversible reaction.

definition.val: An information content entity that represents the relation between the amount of substances that take part in a reaction or form a compound (typically a ratio of whole integers).
An information content entity that describes the number of molecules is taking part in a reaction.
A flux inequality constraint that limits the upper or lower value that a flux may assume.

comments: This parameter may be determined experimentally, or may be the result of theoretical investigation.

definition.val: A data item to describe a dataset or a variable, and it is generated by a calculation on set of observed data.

A statistic that is a measure of variation which correspond to the average distance from the mean of the data set to any given point of that dataset. It also corresponds to the square root of its variance.

comments: It can be for a random variable, statistical population, data set, or probability distribution.

definition.val: A statistic which defines an range of values in which a measurement or trial falls corresponding to a given probability.
A data item that is required to run a fluxomics investigation.
A data transformation that performs statistical inference to decide whether the data provide sufficient evidence to reject a particular hypothesis.
A statistical hypothesis test that aims to evaluate if a sample distribution can be considered equivalent to a theoretical distribution used as input.
A statistical hypothesis test that the sampling distribution of the test statistic is a chi-square distribution when the null hypothesis is true, or any in which this is asymptotically true.
The data transformation that finds parameter values (the model parameter estimates) most compatible with the data as judged by the model.
A data transformation that is estimating properties of an estimator (such as its variance) by measuring those properties when sampling from an approximating distribution.

An information content entity which is a formalization of relationships between variables in the form of mathematical equations. A statistical model describes how one or more random variables are related to one or more other variables. The model is statistical as the variables are not deterministically but stochastically related.
An information content entity that is a rectangular array of numbers, which are called entries of the matrix.

An information content entity that represents a set of process conditions, grouping relevant process control variables and process measurement variables, describing the environmental and physicochemical conditions under which cells are cultivated.
A measurement unit label which represents a standard measurement occurrence of a process per unit time.
A measurement unit label which is a standardised quantity of an element or compound with uniform composition.
A measurement unit label which is a standard measure of the dimension in which events occur in sequence.
A measurement unit label which represents a standard measurement of how much of a given substance there is mixed with another substance.
An information content entity that is the formal representation of a calculus linking parameters and variables of a model.
An atom transition that represents an alternative atom transition of the original reaction.

basicPropertyValues.val: my brain is part of my body (continuant parthood, two material entities)

this day is part of this year (occurrent parthood)
Everything is part of itself. Any part of any part of a thing is itself part of that thing. Two distinct things cannot be part of each other.

Occurrents are not subject to change and so parthood between occurrents holds for all the times that the part exists. Many continuants are subject to change, so parthood between continuants will only hold at certain times, but this is difficult to specify in OWL. See http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ro/docs/temporal-semantics/

Parthood requires the part and the whole to have compatible classes: only an occurrent can be part of an occurrent; only a process can be part of a process; only a continuant can be part of a continuant; only an independent continuant can be part of an independent continuant; only an immaterial entity can be part of an immaterial entity; only a specifically dependent continuant can be part of a specifically dependent continuant; only a generically dependent continuant can be part of a generically dependent continuant. (This list is not exhaustive.)

A continuant cannot be part of an occurrent: use 'participates in'. An occurrent cannot be part of a continuant: use 'has participant'. A material entity cannot be part of an immaterial entity: use 'has location'. A specifically dependent continuant cannot be part of an independent continuant: use 'inheres in'. An independent continuant cannot be part of a specifically dependent continuant: use 'bearer of'.

basicPropertyValues.val:
2012-04-05: 
Barry Smith

The official OBI definition, explaining the meaning of a class or property: 'Shall be Aristotelian, formalized and normalized. Can be augmented with colloquial definitions'  is terrible.

Can you fix to something like:

A statement of necessary and sufficient conditions explaining the meaning of an expression referring to a class or property.

Alan Ruttenberg

Your proposed definition is a reasonable candidate, except that it is very common that necessary and sufficient conditions are not given. Mostly they are necessary, occasionally they are necessary and sufficient or just sufficient. Often they use terms that are not themselves defined and so they effectively can't be evaluated by those criteria. 

On the specifics of the proposed definition:

We don't have definitions of 'meaning' or 'expression' or 'property'. For 'reference' in the intended sense I think we use the term 'denotation'. For 'expression', I think we you mean symbol, or identifier. For 'meaning' it differs for class and property. For class we want documentation that let's the intended reader determine whether an entity is instance of the class, or not. For property we want documentation that let's the intended reader determine, given a pair of potential relata, whether the assertion that the relation holds is true. The 'intended reader' part suggests that we also specify who, we expect, would be able to understand the definition, and also generalizes over human and computer reader to include textual and logical definition. 

Personally, I am more comfortable weakening definition to documentation, with instructions as to what is desirable. 

We also have the outstanding issue of how to aim different definitions to different audiences. A clinical audience reading chebi wants a different sort of definition documentation/definition from a chemistry trained audience, and similarly there is a need for a definition that is adequate for an ontologist to work with.
